core.title: Suppress close-the-loop for docs-only feedback-loop features only via the inline marker on the feature's kind declaration
core.given: A feature whose declared kind is feedback-loop and whose deliverable is documentation only
core.when: the planner wants to opt the feature out of the close-the-loop rule
core.then: Write the opt-out of the close-the-loop rule inline on the feature's kind declaration line, exactly in the profile's suppression-marker syntax, naming the close-the-loop rule, with a valid expiry date.
prefer: Use the stack's suppression marker (the inline opt-out for docs-only feedback-loop features) with a concrete expiry date so the relief expires.
avoid: Suppressing close-the-loop on a feedback-loop feature that is not docs-only.
Placing the suppression anywhere other than inline on the feature's kind declaration line, or omitting the suppressed rule id or the expiry date.
core.why: Docs-only feedback-loop features have no runtime loop to close, so a dated, inline, rule-specific opt-out is the sanctioned hatch that keeps the relief visible and time-bounded.
evidence: The feature's kind declaration line carries the suppression marker naming the close-the-loop rule, with a valid expiry date.
The suppressed feature's scope is documentation only.
verification: A check verifies that any suppression of the close-the-loop rule on a feature is the profile's suppression marker, written inline on the feature's kind declaration line, naming the close-the-loop rule, with a valid expiry date; a misplaced, incomplete or undated marker fails.

The marker's exact syntax is a stack-wide profile pattern carrying a suppressed-rule-id placeholder; this rule's own ids, its term id, and the concrete rule id of the close-the-loop rule are realization details (profile marker syntax plus the reference realization); the core check treats them generically.
'Docs-only' has no mechanical test: judging the feature's scope requires reading the feature, so that activation condition is llm_judged and a purely textual check cannot establish it.

The suppression relieves exactly the close-the-loop rule, until the expiry date. This rule's permission does not police misuse: a suppression marker on a feedback-loop feature that is not docs-only is caught by the close-the-loop rule's own check, not by this rule.

values: planner intends to opt the feature out of close-the-loop (marker not yet written)
suppression marker for the close-the-loop rule added or present on the feature's kind declaration line

fires: A planner authors or edits a docs-only feature of kind feedback-loop and intends to opt it out of the close-the-loop rule, before any marker is written.
A docs-only feedback-loop feature carries (or gains) a suppression marker for the close-the-loop rule.
doesNotFire: A feature whose declared kind is not feedback-loop.
A docs-only feedback-loop feature that neither carries a suppression marker nor is being opted out (close-the-loop applies normally).
A feedback-loop feature that is not docs-only: this permission does not activate; any suppression marker there is a misuse to be caught by the close-the-loop rule's own check, not by this rule.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack-wide syntax of a time-boxed suppression of one rule: a marker pattern with a suppressed-rule-id placeholder and a concrete expiry date. This rule requires its instance naming the close-the-loop rule, written inline on the feature's kind declaration line; the concrete suppressed rule id is filled in from the realization, not from the profile.
Where (and with what syntax) a feature artifact declares its kind; the line to which an inline rule suppression attaches.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the `kind:` line of the planner feature file (e.g. `kind: feedback-loop`)

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kind that is a planner feature file, so activation can identify the files this rule applies to.
profileRequirements.bunValue: feature — planner feature files, identifiable by path/kind

bunOnly.text: Write the suppression inline on the kind: line exactly as `kind: feedback-loop  # atdd:suppress(planner.smoke.feedback-loop-close-the-loop) UNTIL=YYYY-MM-DD`.
bunOnly.reason: The verbatim line combines the stack's kind-line syntax, the suppression-marker pattern, this realization's close-the-loop rule id (the profile marker's <rule_id> placeholder) and the UNTIL field; the core composes the same obligation from the profile's suppression-marker pattern and kind-declaration line, and only the reference realization renders this exact string.

bunOnly.text: The feature's kind: line contains `# atdd:suppress(planner.smoke.feedback-loop-close-the-loop) UNTIL=YYYY-MM-DD` with a valid date.
bunOnly.reason: The verbatim marker instance instantiates the profile pattern with this realization's close-the-loop rule id.

bunOnly.text: Term suppression_marker: inline opt-out for docs-only feedback-loop features. Syntax: `kind: feedback-loop  # atdd:suppress(planner.smoke.feedback-loop-close-the-loop) UNTIL=YYYY-MM-DD`.
bunOnly.reason: The term id and the fully instantiated syntax are realization details; the core's verification describes the check generically against the profile's suppression-marker pattern and kind declaration line.

bunOnly.text: Graph: this rule relieves planner.smoke.feedback-loop-close-the-loop (and planner.feature.feedback-loop-close-the-loop) until the UNTIL date.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete rule ids of this realization's rule graph — including the id that fills the profile marker's suppressed-rule placeholder; the core names the close-the-loop rule generically and keeps the relief scope and time-box in core verification.

neutralityNotes: Method-level concepts kept in the core: 'planner' (author of feature plan artifacts), the feature kind value 'feedback-loop', 'docs-only', and 'close-the-loop' (the suppressed rule, named generically; its concrete ids are bunOnly). All stack syntax is profile-supplied: the suppression marker (enforcement.suppression_marker, recorded as the stack-wide pattern '# atdd:suppress(<rule_id>) UNTIL=YYYY-MM-DD' with its rule-id placeholder and UNTIL expiry field — single-rule identifiers are realization details per the vocabulary, so the concrete close-the-loop rule id appears only in bunOnly) and the feature kind declaration line (proposed idiom.plan_syntax#feature_kind_declaration). The verbatim suppression line and the rule-graph ids exist only in the Bun reference realization. `unless` is empty in the source, so the core adds none.
